n: *Translator's note:* *Heb* “nine of the hands.” The word “hand” is used here in the sense or a part or portion.

*Text-critical note:* The translation reads מִן־הַשֵּׁלָנִי (min hashelani, “from the Shelahite”) rather than the MT reading בֶּן־הַשִּׁלֹנִי (ben hashiloni, “the son of the Shilionite”). See 1 Chr 9:5.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “those behind him.” Some scholars emend the text to וְאֶחָיו (veʾekhayv, “his brothers”).
*Text-critical note:* The translation reads with the LXX וְאֶחָיו (veʾekhayv, “and his brothers”) rather than the MT reading וַאֲחֵיהֶם (vaʾakhehem, “and their brothers”).

*Text-critical note:* The translation reads with the Lucianic Greek recension and Vulgate הַתְּהִלָּה (hattehillah, “the praise”) rather than the MT reading הַתְּחִלָּה (hattekhillah, “the beginning”).
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the temple attendants.” The pronoun “them” has been substituted in the translation for stylistic reasons.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the commandment of the king was over them.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “a thing of a day in its day.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to the hand of the king.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “its daughters.” So also in vv. 27, 28, 30, and 31.

*Text-critical note:* The translation reads with a few medieval Hebrew MSS and the Syriac Peshitta וּמִבְּנֵי (umibbene, “and some of the descendants of”; cf. NLT) rather than the MT reading וּבְנֵי (uvene, “and the sons of”).

*Text-critical note:* *Heb* “from Geba.” It is preferable to delete the preposition “from” read by the MT.

*Text-critical note:* The translation reads וְגֵי (vegey, “and the valley”) rather than the MT reading גֵּי (gey, “the valley”). The original vav (ו) probably dropped out accidentally due to haplography with the final vav on the immediately preceding word.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Ge-harashim,” which could be left untranslated as a place name.
*Text-critical note:* Most Hebrew MSS read “Ginnethoi”; the present translation follows a number of Hebrew MSS and the Vulgate (cf. Neh 12:16 and NIV, NCV, NLT).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “heads” (so also in v. 12).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “brothers” (also in vv. 8, 9, 24, 36).
*Text-critical note:* The translation reads וְעֻנִּי (veʿunni) with the *Qere* rather than וְעֻנּוֹ (veʿunno) of the MT *Kethib*.

*Text-critical note:* The present translation reads with the LXX לְמַלּוּךְ (lemallukh) rather than לִמְלוּכִי (limlukhi) of the *Kethib* (by dittography) or לִמְלִיכוּ (limlikhu) of the *Qere*.

*Text-critical note:* Most Hebrew MSS read “Shebaniah” (cf. KJV, NAB, NASB, NRSV, CEV); the present translation follows the reading of some Hebrew MSS, some LXX MSS, and the Syriac (cf. Neh 12:3 and NIV, NCV, NLT).

*Text-critical note:* The present translation reads with the Lucianic Greek recension and the Syriac Peshitta לִמְרֵמוֹת (limremot, cf. NAB, NIV, NCV, NLT “Meremoth”) rather than the MT reading לִמְרָיוֹת (limrayot, cf. KJV, NASB, NRSV, CEV “Meraioth”). Cf. v. 3.

*Text-critical note:* The present translation (along with most English versions) reads with the *Qere* and the Syriac Peshitta לְעִדּוֹא (leʿiddoʾ, “Iddo”) rather than the MT reading לַעֲדָיָא (laʿadayaʾ) which probably arose through graphic confusion. Cf. v. 4.
*Translator's note:* Or “of Miniamin,…; of Moadiah, Piltai,” where the name of the leader of the family of Miniamin has dropped out of the text due to a problem in transmission.
*Text-critical note:* The present translation reads סַלּוּ (sallu, cf. NAB, NIV, NCV, NLT “Sallu”) rather than the MT reading סַלַּי (sallai, cf. KJV, NASB, NRSV, CEV “Sallai”) . Cf. v. 7.
*Translator's note:* Some scholars delete these words, regarding them as a later scribal addition to the text.
*Translator's note:* Or “the Book of the Official Records”; NRSV “the Book of the Annals”; NLT “The Book of History.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “from all their places.” The words “they lived” are implied.
*Text-critical note:* The translation reads וְהָאַחַת הֹלֶכֶת (vehaʾakhat holekhet, “and one was proceeding”) rather than the MT reading וְתַהֲלֻכֹת (vetahalukhot, “and processions”).
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “some of the sons of the priests.”

*Translator's note:* Or “prescribed by” (NIV, NLT); TEV “of the kind played by.” The precise relationship of these musical instruments to David is not clear.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “was before them.”

*Text-critical note:* The translation reads הוֹלֶכֶת (holekhet, “was proceeding”) rather than the MT הַהוֹלֶכֶת (haholekhet, “the one proceeding”). The MT probably reflects dittography—accidental writing of ה (hey) twice instead of once.

*Translator's note:* Or “the Old Gate” (so KJV, NASB, NCV, NRSV).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “they stood.”

*Text-critical note:* The translation reads מִשְּׂדֵי (missede, “from the fields”) rather than the MT reading לִשְׂדֵי (lisde, “to the fields”).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “for Judah.” The words “the people of” have been supplied in the translation for clarity, since “Judah” is a proper name as well as a place name.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “standing.”
*Text-critical note:* With many medieval Hebrew MSS and the ancient versions the translation reads the conjunction (“and”). It is absent in the Leningrad MS that forms the textual basis for *BHS*.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “heads.” The translation reads with the *Qere* the plural רֹאשֵׁי (roʾshe, “heads”) rather than the *Kethib* singular רֹאשׁ (roʾsh, “head”) of the MT.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “a thing of a day in its day.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “were sanctifying.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “ears.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “it was found.” The Hebrew verb is passive.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “bread.” The Hebrew term is generic here, however, referring to more than bread alone.
*Text-critical note:* The translation reads the plural rather than the singular of the MT.
*Translator's note:* On the usage of this Hebrew word see *HALOT* 478-79 s.v. כְּלִי.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and I stood them on their standing.”

*Text-critical note:* Probably one should read with the Lucianic Greek recension, the Syriac Peshitta, and the Vulgate וָאֲצַוֶּה (vaʾatsavveh, “and I commanded”) rather than the rare denominative verb וָאוֹצְרָה (vaʾotserah, “and I appointed over the storeroom”) of the MT.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “be over”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “on their hand.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “brothers.”
*Translator's note:* The words “of all places” are not in the Hebrew text but have been supplied in the translation to indicate the emphasis on Jerusalem.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “your fathers.”

*Translator's note:* The words “like this” are not in the Hebrew text but have been supplied.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the gates of Jerusalem grew dark.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “said” (so also in v. 22).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “caused to stand.”

*Translator's note:* The Hebrew text includes the words “to them,” but they have been excluded from the translation for stylistic reasons.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “I will send a hand on you.”

*Study note:* This statement contains a great deal of restrained humor. The author clearly takes pleasure in the effectiveness of the measures that he had enacted.

*Text-critical note:* One medieval Hebrew MS, the Lucianic Greek recension, and the Syriac Peshitta read the plural הַכֹּהֲנִים (hakkohanim, “the priests”) rather than the singular reading of the MT, הַכְּהֻנָּה (hakkehunnah, “the priesthood”).
*Translator's note:* The words “I also provided for” are not included in the Hebrew text, but are supplied in the translation for the sake of clarity.
